args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding but the implementation used
ROUND_HALF_UP, which rounds 2.665 up to 2.67 instead of down to 2.66.
This caused the nightly test in tests/test_money.py to fail.

Change the quantize call to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN so ties round to the
nearest even cent, as required by FIN-212.

args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented the `ROUND_HALF_UP` rounding mode.

## Fix

Changed the `rounding` argument in `round_money()` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so that ties round to the nearest even cent. Example behavior change:

- `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` now returns `2.66` (banker's rounding) instead of `2.67`
- `round_money(Decimal("2.675"))` still returns `2.68`

This matches the documented intent of the docstring and satisfies FIN-212.

## Testing

CI has been run on this branch (`ci-0001`) and all tests pass, including `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.

Fixes the nightly build failure.
